summary.text: Today, 号 is used as the simplified form of 號, with meanings including mark, sign, symbol, and number. A separate historical entry explains 号 as a painful cry, written with 口 above 丂, which it interprets as breath obstructed beneath the mouth.

formation.text: In the traditional account, 号 is a semantic compound: 口 depicts a mouth, while 丂 is interpreted as breath obstructed above. Together they explain the painful-cry sense. This account does not establish the graph’s earliest construction, and 丂 is not established as a sound component. In the separate graph 號, a traditional analysis assigns 号 the sound role and 虎 the meaning role; a proposed tiger-and-exhaled-breath origin for 號 remains uncertain.

components.text: In the traditional account of 号, 口 depicts the mouth in the explanation of a painful cry.

The traditional account interprets 丂 as breath obstructed beneath 口, completing its explanation of a painful cry. Its role as a depicted element is uncertain, and it is not established as a sound component.

history.text: The traditional dictionary account records 号 as a separate graph formed from 口 above 丂 and meaning “painful cry.” It does not derive this graph from 號.

Catalogues list 號 on Western Zhou bronzes and a separate 号 form on early Warring States Chu bronze. These attestations establish neither graph’s first appearance nor a direct graphic sequence; the catalogues supply no oracle-bone form.
Later writing and dictionaries brought 号 and 號 into overlapping use. Today, 号 serves as the simplified form of 號, while the separate historical graph remains part of the record.
A proposal interprets 號 as originating in a tiger with a line for exhaled air. This remains uncertain: readings of 號 do not recover a historical name for a depicted tiger’s cry.

uncertainties.text: The traditional 口-plus-丂 account explains 号 as a painful cry but does not establish its earliest construction or show 丂 functioning as a sound component.
The catalogues give different attestation points for 号 and 號 without settling their earliest forms or a precise graphic transition.
The proposed tiger-roar origin and graphic sequence for 號 remain uncertain; readings of 號 cannot establish the historical sound of a depicted tiger’s cry.

senses.text: The separate historical dictionary entry for 号 gives this sense. It is an attested lexicographic meaning, not proof of the graph’s hypothetical original meaning.

senses.period: early textual examples cited in dictionaries; surviving witnesses undated here
senses.text: Dictionary-cited examples for 號 include crying and calling. They document meanings associated with 號, not a dated transition from the separate graph 号.
Examples and dictionary commentary associate 號 with names and titles. An extension from calling to what is called is plausible, though its chronology is incomplete.

senses.gloss: command; order; assigned number or sequence
senses.text: Dictionaries record commanding and numbered or ordered uses for 號. They do not give a complete dated path from crying or calling to these senses.
These are modern glosses recorded for 号/號. Their listing does not establish a chronological sequence among them.

developments.text: A name or title can be understood as what is called. Examples and dictionary commentary suggest this extension for 號, though its chronology is incomplete.
Calling can extend to summoning or commanding, but the cited summaries do not establish every step or its date for 號.

limitations.text: Dictionary summaries and modern glosses do not establish first occurrences or a complete chronology. Dates assigned to classical works are not dates of surviving manuscripts.
The cited semantic history chiefly concerns 號 and its later overlap with 号; it does not establish that the separate historical graph 号 had all these senses before the forms converged.
The evidence does not establish how the current mark, sign, symbol, and number senses relate chronologically to the historical senses of 號.

overview.text: Today, 号 is used for mark, sign, symbol, or number as the simplified form of 號. In a separate traditional account, 口 (mouth) above 丂 (obstructed breath) explains a painful cry; that account does not establish the graph’s earliest construction.

components.text: In the separate historical account of 号, this is the mouth in the traditional painful-cry explanation.
Traditionally, this shape represents breath trying to emerge but blocked above; its role as a depicted element in 号 is uncertain.

takeaway.text: Today’s use of 号 for 號 reflects later graphic convergence; the historical entry for 号 as a painful cry is separate.

relationships.text: In the traditional account of 号, 口 depicts the mouth in a painful-cry scene.
Later use brought 号 into use as a variant of 號; today 号 is used as its simplified form. This graphic relationship is distinct from the older separate entry for 号.
